clue.text: Lords official with dark-skinned staff

parts.note: black describes dark skin
a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: A peer's attendant carries a stick of dark wood.
explanation.walkthrough: Black Rod is the officer of the House of Lords who summons the Commons to hear the monarch's speech.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gentleman Usher of the Black Rod is a ceremonial officer of Britain's upper parliamentary chamber.

clue.text: Short letters not written on the beach

parts.note: Litt. is the abbreviation for letters, as in the degree D.Litt.
oral means spoken rather than written

explanation.surface: Brief notes go unwritten at the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: The held text adds 'times,' which the printed page does not have.
explanation.definitionFit: A littoral is the shore zone of a sea or lake, the strip of coast where sand meets water.

clue.text: Diurnal insect of a green colour

parts.note: cabbage green is a shade, and a cabbage is a green vegetable
white is a colour

explanation.surface: A daytime bug is described by its leafy green hue.
explanation.walkthrough: The cabbage white is a common butterfly; 'diurnal' (active by day) separates butterflies from moths.
explanation.definitionFit: This butterfly flies by day and lays eggs on brassica leaves, a familiar garden pest.

clue.text: Advance payment can produce the right trainee

indicators.note: the letters can be made into something new, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Paying ahead might yield a properly trained apprentice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can produce' rearranges R (right) plus TRAINEE; 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A retainer is a fee paid upfront to secure someone's services, such as a lawyer's.

clue.text: Gone to object? It won't get you anywhere

parts.note: gone can mean dead, departed
an end is an aim or object

explanation.surface: A departed goal leads nowhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A cul-de-sac or futile course of action leads nowhere, so it gets you no further.

clue.text: Hairdresser's roller

definitions.meaning: one who combs hair, read as 'hairdresser is'
a long curling wave breaking on a shore

explanation.surface: A stylist's curler.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally one who combs, and also a long breaking sea wave.

clue.text: Stop, being lame

definitions.meaning: to cease or come to a standstill
an archaic word for limping or crippled

explanation.surface: Halting because of an injured leg.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb for cease moving, and an old adjective meaning limping, as in 'the halt and the lame'.

clue.text: Emotional expression from doctor in rush operation

indicators.note: the doctor sits inside the run of rush plus operation

parts.note: to tear is to rush or dash

explanation.surface: A medic in a hurried surgery shows his feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: The container indicator is 'in': the doctor goes inside the run of rush plus operation, though the surface reads it as a medic at work in a hurried operation.
explanation.definitionFit: A single tear running down the cheek shows sadness or strong feeling.

clue.text: Pull out elegant love letters

indicators.note: the letters of the preceding words are taken loose and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone draws out a stylish romantic correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters' asks for the letters of ELEGANT plus O (love) rearranged; 'love letters' is the surface trap.
explanation.definitionFit: To lengthen something is to stretch or draw it out.

clue.text: Try to return clubs

indicators.note: returning sends the word back on itself, so it is read backwards

parts.note: bats are clubs used in games

explanation.surface: An attempt to give the golf clubs back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' turns BATS backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a stab at something is to have a go or attempt it.

clue.text: Black lustful goat giving sauce

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
randy is British slang for lustful
a butter is something that butts, as a goat does

explanation.surface: A dark, lecherous billy goat is turned into a dressing.
explanation.walkthrough: Brandy butter is the rich sauce served with British Christmas pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet hard sauce of brandy, sugar and creamed fat is spooned over festive puddings.

clue.text: A harmless bouncer

parts.note: not a nightclub doorman who ejects people, but someone who springs up and down on a stretched mat for fun

explanation.surface: A gentle doorman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bouncer' suggests a nightclub doorman; harmless because this one only jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: A gymnast who performs on a sprung canvas frame is literally a person who bounces.

clue.text: State nothing right, say nothing new

parts.note: nought, written as the letter O
e.g. means for example, which 'say' also means
a second nought, O

explanation.surface: A politician declares nothing correct and says nothing fresh.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregon is one of the fifty US states, on the Pacific coast.

clue.text: Island's rebuff to royal reporter

indicators.note: a rebuff turns something back, so the island name is read backwards

parts.note: Arran is an island off western Scotland
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for royal, as in RN

explanation.surface: An island rejects a monarch's approach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuff' turns ARRAN backwards; Arran is a Scottish island in the Firth of Clyde.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrator is someone who recounts or relates events, a teller of a story.

clue.text: Fancy being let down in the margins of the fairway!

indicators.note: the lowered word sits between the edges of the fairway
margins are a word's edges, its first and last letters

parts.note: to lower is to let down

explanation.surface: A golf course edge is planted with blooms, lowering the tone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts LOWER between F and Y, the first and last letters of 'fairway'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornate, overdecorated language is described as fancy or florid.

clue.text: Capped F.A. official upset when overridden

indicators.note: in a down answer upset turns the word upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: a ref, a referee in Football Association matches
ruled, as when a decision is overruled or overridden

explanation.surface: A football referee is overruled and upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns REF backwards. The F.A. is England's Football Association.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitted with a metal cap or band at the tip, as on a walking stick.

clue.text: Fill cavity as a temporary measure

parts.note: to stop a hole is to fill it
a gap is an opening or hollow

explanation.surface: A dentist plugs a tooth hollow for now.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopgap is a makeshift substitute used until something better is ready.

clue.text: Experiment underground needed for chemical analysis

parts.note: a test is an experiment
the Tube is London's underground railway

explanation.surface: A trial on the subway is required for a laboratory investigation.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is the London Underground.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass tube closed at one end is lab equipment used in chemistry experiments.

clue.text: Girl runs away in mischief from studious person

indicators.note: the shortened name sits inside the word for mischief

parts.note: Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and folly

indicators.note: goes away signals removal of the runs letter

parts.note: Esther is a girl's name
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A young woman flees from trouble, away from a bookish type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs away' is a deletion: 'runs' is cricket's R and 'away' takes it off the girl. 'in' is the container. Ate, the Greek goddess of mischief, is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: An aesthete devotes himself to the study and appreciation of art and beauty.

clue.text: He's out to score goals

parts.note: reads as a footballer keen to score, but is also someone who has walked out of work in a dispute

explanation.surface: A forward is set on finding the net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' is the trade-union sense, on strike; the forward who scores is the other sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A forward in football whose job is scoring, and also a worker who has downed tools.

clue.text: Stayer: is faltering — tiredness, mostly

indicators.note: something faltering is unsteady, so the letters are shaken into a new order
most of the word is kept, dropping its last letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A long-distance runner falters, worn out and nearly spent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last S of 'tiredness'; 'faltering' rearranges the remaining TIREDNES; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A resident is one who lives or remains in a place rather than passing through.

clue.text: Cover up in French shawl

parts.note: en is French for in
a wrap is a shawl

explanation.surface: Someone bundles up in a Parisian stole.
explanation.definitionFit: To enwrap is to envelop or swathe something completely.

clue.text: With the odds secure, spend freely

parts.note: SP is the starting price, the betting odds on a horse
to lash is to tie down or secure

explanation.surface: Once the betting price is safe, a gambler lavishes money.
explanation.walkthrough: SP, starting price, is the final odds offered on a horse at the off.
explanation.definitionFit: To splash out is to lavish money on something.

clue.text: Liability accepted with a subscription

definitions.meaning: a risk has been guaranteed by an insurer who takes it on
having a signature or writing set beneath, the old sense of subscribe

explanation.surface: An insurer takes on a risk and signs at the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Insurance terms for a guaranteed risk, and literally having something inscribed below.

clue.text: Platform needed for a short girl

indicators.note: short means the name loses its last letter

parts.note: Daisy is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A small woman needs a stage to stand on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts the last letter of DAISY.
explanation.definitionFit: A dais is a raised stage at one end of a hall, for speakers.

clue.text: Fish that is tailless

indicators.note: without its tail means the last letter is removed

parts.note: id est is the Latin for that is, abbreviated i.e.

explanation.surface: A fish has lost its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailless' removes the last T from ID EST, the Latin behind i.e.
explanation.definitionFit: The ide is a European freshwater carp-family species, and this is its plural.

clue.text: English fighter with the speed to get to America, perhaps

parts.note: a MiG is a Russian fighter plane
rate means speed

explanation.surface: An English pilot flies fast enough to reach the States.
explanation.definitionFit: To move abroad permanently, with the New World as an example destination.

clue.text: Turning green — not from a dose of radiation

indicators.note: turning changes the order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Going green from a heavy exposure is not good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' rearranges GREEN plus NOT; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The roentgen is an old unit measuring exposure to X-rays or gamma rays.
